config.title: JWT Storage & Decode in React

intro.title: JWT Storage & Decode in React
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular application that stores a JSON Web Token (JWT) in the browser's localStorage and decodes it to display user information. You will learn the core concept of managing authentication state and securely handling tokens on the client side. The main technologies involved are Angular services for logic, TypeScript for type safety, and the jwt-decode library for parsing the token. By the end, you'll understand how to persist user sessions and extract data from JWTs in a structured Angular project.
intro.usecase: In real-world Angular applications, JWT storage and decoding is essential for user authentication and authorization. This pattern appears in dashboards where user roles determine accessible features, in e-commerce platforms that persist login sessions, and in admin panels that display user-specific data. Developers implement JWT handling to secure API calls, manage user sessions across page refreshes, and personalize UI elements based on decoded token claims like user roles or permissions.

objectives: Construct an Angular service to manage JWT token storage and retrieval
Implement token decoding logic using the jwt-decode library in a TypeScript service
Configure Angular HTTP interceptors to automatically attach JWT tokens to outgoing requests
Initialize and bind decoded token data to Angular component properties for display
Integrate token validation checks within Angular route guards for protected routes
Manipulate token storage using browser localStorage with proper error handling
Render user information from decoded JWT tokens in Angular template views

steps.hint: Use localStorage.setItem('jwtToken', this.token) inside the method body.
